acceptanceCriteria: Each of the four sites signals before the reap or carries a documented, tested reason; a regression test per changed site that fails with the old order.
body: Found by the V1-1036 lane audit on 2026-10-09 (base b2a0b8c6, Darwin arm64, code inspection; no runtime reproduction). Sites outside V1-1036's listed scope still signal a process group after its leader can be reaped, so a reused group ID can be signalled: (1) internal/tasks/store/lease_gate.go execute via killGate: the timer, AfterFunc and overflow kills race cmd.Wait, so one can land after the reap; candidate fix is the groupreap Contain/Stop/Wait adoption V1-1036 applied to the pool runners. (2) internal/dashboard/repository/process_wait_linux.go reaps first, then probes, then terminates or forces the numeric group; needs the same pre-reap residue observation V1-1036 adds for the work runner (the Darwin path is compliant). (3) internal/opencodequalification/terminal_posix.go sends its deferred group SIGTERM and final SIGKILL after child.Wait reaps. (4) internal/testsupport/pipedrain_unix.go test cleanup sends kill(-leader) after the reap (test-only, low risk). Expected: every group signal is sent while the leader is unreaped, or the site documents and tests why a post-reap signal cannot hit a reused group. Details: docs/build-log/2026-10-09-v1-1036-post-reap-group-signals.md once batch P lands.

Tests named in the PR: TestPGOV0009BatchCommandSendsNoGroupSignalAfterTheReap, TestPGOV0009ProcGroupLiveUsesTheQuietProof. Doc gates, repin check, independent review and dogfood bind/check/seal reported PASS in the PR. make gate NOT_RUN (owner scoped-work preference); native claim unavailable (COVERAGE_UNKNOWN/RESOURCE_COLLISION).
